full.description: This is a micrograph showing a skin biopsy with a distinct column of parakeratosis known as a cornoid lamella wedged into the epidermis. The underlying epidermis exhibits a focal loss of the granular cell layer and some dyskeratosis. These histological features are characteristic of porokeratosis. The image captures the diagnostic scanning-to-medium magnification perspective typically used to identify this lesion.

Plexiform fibrohistiocytic tumor. (A) plexiform fibrohistiocytic tumor has an infiltrative, plexiform growth pattern composed of discrete nodules of histiocytic cells and fascicles of myofibroblastic cells. (B) the nodules are composed of round to slightly spindled histiocytic cells. the surrounding myofibroblastic proliferation may be reminiscent of fibromatosis.

Minimal deviation endocervical adenocarcinoma. Complex, irregular glands infiltrate the cervical stroma in a disorderly fashion (A). An irregular branching gland is lined by cells with abundant intracellular mucin (B). The cells lining the neoplastic glands are columnar with small hyperchromatic nuclei and rare mitoses (C). However, notice the presence of overt malignant glands next to the better-differentiated areas (D).
